questions.q: Why does the validation script write its results to a dw.DataQualityLog table instead of only printing to the console?
options: Console output is automatically saved by Windows regardless
A console print is only visible at the exact moment the script runs; a log table lets a human check results later, on their own schedule, with ordinary SQL
SQL Server does not allow Python to print to a console
Printing to a console is slower than writing to a table
questions.explain: At 2 AM, nobody is watching a terminal. A queryable log table means 'show me every failed check in the last 30 days' is just a WHERE clause.

questions.q: Why does logging to a SQL table beat a plain text log file for this specific job?
options: Text files cannot be created on Windows
It's queryable with the exact same SQL skills already used throughout this capstone, instead of requiring a script to parse log files by hand
SQL tables take up less disk space than text files
Text files cannot store timestamps
questions.explain: A table in the dw schema can be filtered and sorted with ordinary SQL, the same skill set used everywhere else in this warehouse, rather than parsing unstructured text.

questions.q: Why must the validation task be scheduled to run strictly AFTER the nightly warehouse refresh finishes, not before or during it?
options: Running it before would validate yesterday's data and call it done, defeating the entire purpose of checking tonight's load
Task Scheduler does not support running two tasks in sequence
The warehouse refresh job depends on the validation script to start
It makes no real difference as long as both tasks run once a day
questions.explain: The validation step has to be the last step in the nightly chain so a logged PASS or FAIL is actually about that night's freshly loaded data.

questions.q: In Windows Task Scheduler, which setting specifically helps if the machine was off at the scheduled 2 AM run time?
options: Run with highest privileges
Run task as soon as possible after a scheduled start is missed
Stop the task if it runs longer than 3 days
Allow task to be run on demand
questions.explain: This setting ensures the check still runs once the machine is back on, instead of silently skipping that night's validation entirely.

questions.q: What does a human actually have to do on a normal night, once this scheduled logging pipeline is running?
options: Manually re-run the Python script every morning to confirm it worked
Nothing — the check runs unattended, and a human is only pulled in when dw.DataQualityLog shows a failed row
Manually copy the log file to a shared drive every day
Restart SQL Server before the scheduled task runs
questions.explain: The whole point of scheduling and logging is that the check runs with zero human involvement on a normal night — a human only investigates when a failure actually appears in the log.
